title: The Sparrow
text:
Turgenev tells of walking back from hunting along an avenue in his garden, with his dog running ahead of him. Suddenly the dog slowed down and began creeping forward, as if it had scented game.

Looking along the path, he saw a young sparrow with yellow at the corners of its beak and down on its head. It had fallen from its nest, which the wind was shaking in the birches overhead. It sat motionless on the ground, its little wings helplessly spread.

The dog was approaching it slowly when an old sparrow dropped from a nearby tree like a stone, right in front of the dog's nose. All its feathers ruffled, distorted, with a desperate and pitiful chirping, it hopped twice toward the open, toothy jaws. It had flung itself down to save its young, to shield the chick with its own body. Its whole small body was trembling with terror and its voice was hoarse, but it would not move.

To the sparrow, the narrator says, the dog must have seemed a giant monster. Still it could not stay safe in its tree. The dog stopped and backed away. Turgenev called his dog off and walked away, filled with reverence for that small, heroic bird and its love, which he felt was stronger than death.
lesson: Love for a child can make the weakest creature fearless. Do not underestimate what a parent will face for the sake of their young.
people: The narrator, his dog, a mother sparrow, a fledgling
source: Ivan Turgenev, Poems in Prose (Senilia), The Sparrow (Vorobei), 1878
